content.text: The secret doesn't actually include the password hash, despite the comment.

candidates.explanation: The comment says the per-user JWT secret embeds the current password hash so reset links stop verifying once the password changes. The code actually returns `forgotSecret + user.email`. Changing the password doesn't change the secret, so a used reset token still verifies until it expires. The same link can then be used to set another password.

After verification, the token is not invalidated in any way. There is no stored single-use marker and nothing else ties the token to the password state. So it relies entirely on getForgotSecret changing after the password update, and that doesn't happen.

fix.description: Include the user's current password hash in the signing secret, e.g. `return `${forgotSecret}${user.password ?? ''}`;`. This requires that usersService.findById returns the password field. Use the same value in forgotPassword and resetPassword. Once the password changes, old tokens fail verification.

The code actually returns `forgotSecret + user.email`. Changing the password doesn't change the secret, so a used reset token still verifies until it expires. The same link can then be used to set another password.

After verification, the token is not invalidated in any way. There is no stored single-use marker and nothing else ties the token to the password state. So it relies entirely on getForgotSecret changing after the password update, and that doesn't happen.

fix.description: Include the user's current password hash in the signing secret, e.g. `return `${forgotSecret}${user.password ?? ''}`;`. This requires that usersService.findById returns the password field. Use the same value in forgotPassword and resetPassword. Once the password changes, old tokens fail verification.
